commands.description:
Add dialects to rootform.lock. Each source is a local directory (./path),
a registry reference with a tag or digest, or the owner of an embedded dialect
that the project excluded.

Rootform compiles and verifies every source, records its exact identity,
and writes rootform.lock once, or not at all. A registry source is
installed in the Rootform home. A tag is resolved once and never
recorded.

A dialect whose owner is embedded in Rootform replaces the embedded
one only with --replace.

When the project vendors this family under .rootform/, the vendored
copy changes together with rootform.lock.

The summary goes to standard output. Diagnostics go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  rootform.lock matches the request
  1  nothing was written because a source or the result is invalid
  2  the command was used incorrectly
commands.examples:
rootform add dialects ./dialects/payments
  rootform add dialects \
    registry.example.com/acme/dialects:dialect-payments-0.1.0
  rootform add dialects ./dialects/aws --replace

commands.description:
Show how one instance was interpreted: its rule and concept, the facts
it takes part in with their evidence, each closure outcome, its
dependencies and its diagnostics. A declaration address explains every
instance of that declaration.

--input accepts a plan JSON, a state JSON, a saved Rootform document, or
'-' for standard input. A plan or state is compiled with the project's
Dialects; a Rootform document is read as it is. --stage selects the
stage; the default is the document's default stage.

The text or JSON explanation goes to standard output. Diagnostics go to
standard error.

Exit status:
  0  the result was explained
  1  the named instance or definition was not found
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no explanation could be decided
commands.examples:
rootform explain architecture google_compute_network.vpc --input plan.json
  rootform explain architecture 'aws_instance.web["a"]' --input state.json
  rootform explain architecture aws_vpc.main --input plan.json --stage refreshed
  rootform explain architecture aws_vpc.main --input analysis.json --format json

commands.description:
Prepare an existing rootform.lock and materialize the project's exact
non-embedded selections (dialects and Policy Pack sources) locally.

init is explicit: it never detects providers, selects another version,
or writes rootform.lock. With --locked the existing rootform.lock is
required and valid; without it, a missing lock is an empty selection
and an existing lock is always preserved. Embedded dialects ship
inside the release set and are never acquired. When network access is
available and not disabled by --offline, init fetches only the exact
manifest digests already pinned by rootform.lock.

Path defaults to . and is both the project and Terraform or OpenTofu
root. Machine JSON goes to standard output. Diagnostics and verbose
detail go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  preparation completed
  1  preparation failed
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  no deterministic preparation was available
commands.examples:
rootform init
  rootform init ./infra
  rootform init ./infra --locked --offline
  rootform init ./infra --no-input
  rootform init ./infra --format json

With no name, every loaded dialect is included. The default listing
names one dialect per line, -o wide adds version, origin and how
much each dialect declares, and -o json carries the exact version,
origin and content digest of every selection.

error.

  3  the selected definitions could not be read

  rootform list dialects -o wide
  rootform list dialects google aws

commands.summary: Analyze a plan or state, or open a saved Rootform document
commands.description:
Analyze a Terraform or OpenTofu plan JSON or state JSON with the project's
Dialects, or open a saved Rootform document without analyzing it again. The
input kind comes from its content, and '-' reads standard input. Export a
plan with "terraform show -json plan.tfplan" and a state with
"terraform show -json"; a configuration directory is not an input.

A plan made with a prior state also reports drift: what changed outside
Terraform or OpenTofu between the recorded and the refreshed state. --diff
compares two inputs, such as a state and a later plan, or two saved
documents.

By default run serves the result on a loopback address and opens a browser
until interrupted. --no-serve writes the requested files and exits.

The summary goes to standard output, or the --format output when no file is
written. Progress, warnings, the server address and failures go to standard
error. Each -o file takes its format from its extension: .json (the Rootform
document), .md, .txt, .sarif or .html. Every file is rendered before any is
written.

Exit status:
  0  analyzed, and every selected policy passed
  1  a selected policy was violated
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the input was refused, or a policy was indeterminate or decided nothing
  4  a file could not be written or the server could not start
commands.examples:
rootform run plan.json
  terraform show -json plan.tfplan | rootform run -
  rootform run state.json --no-serve -o analysis.json
  rootform run plan.json --no-serve -o report.md -o results.sarif
  rootform run before.json --diff after.json --no-serve

commands.description:
Analyze Dialect fixtures and compare the Rootform documents they
produce with the recorded ones. A fixture is a directory holding one
plan.json or state.json export and an analysis.golden document; the
project at the test directory selects the Dialects. A plan.tfplan saved
plan beside plan.json must verify against it, and its configuration
snapshot then contributes the facts that follow references.

A golden records the analysis with only the Dialect definitions it
reaches. The comparison ignores which Rootform version and which Dialect
versions recorded it. With --update, test writes the produced golden for
every case that differs, and for a directory holding an export but no
golden yet.

With no directory, test reads the current directory. Text or JSON results
go to standard output. Diagnostics go to standard error.

Exit status:
  0  every selected fixture passed or, with --update, was recorded
  1  at least one fixture differed or encountered an error
  2  the command was used incorrectly
  3  the run could not start or be reported, or no fixtures matched
commands.examples:
rootform test
  rootform test ./fixtures
  rootform test ./fixtures --run cloud-sql
  rootform test ./fixtures --format json
  rootform test ./fixtures --update
